## Context / Problem

The multi-project model changes things a reader currently learns from the docs as single-project
facts: `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:74` presents `project` as one config line and has no section on
multiple projects, `docs/config.md:216-260` documents the `[jira]` block as a single scalar project,
and `docs/migrations.md` describes the ensure registry without the two units this epic adds. A user
upgrading a client store also needs to know what the new `required_capabilities` entry means for
older binaries in their fleet. None of that is documented by the implementation stories, which own
code and tests only.

## Approach

Document the shipped behaviour and record the architectural decision. The ADR is warranted rather
than decorative because two decisions here are load-bearing, non-obvious, and expensive to reverse:
that the project set is a property of the **store** rather than of a repo, and that the legacy
migration writes **no ticket events**. Both were chosen against plausible alternatives — per-repo
project lists and an EDIT-per-ticket backfill — and a future reader who does not know why will be
tempted back toward them.

The ADR is `docs/adr/0097-*` — the next free number after `0096-pandoc-corpus-verification-boundary.md` (the current maximum; the earlier `0062` slot is already taken by `0062-pagination-stall-aborts-past-fail-open.md`).
It records the shared-`prev_snapshot` reasoning for store ownership, the short-lock-budget reasoning
for the event-free migration, and the conditional-stamp reasoning for compatibility. It also notes the
relationship to ADR 0060, whose churn constraint the mapping satisfies by construction.

Documentation updates cover the mapping and its `bridge projects` verb, the tri-state project field,
the repos field, the two ensure units, and the upgrade note for fleets running mixed binary versions.

## Scope

- `docs/adr/0097-many-to-many-tracker-projects.md` (new)
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`
- `docs/config.md`
- `docs/migrations.md`
- `docs/user-guide.md`
- `docs/ticket-model.md`

## Testing

No `## Testing` section beyond this note: this story adds no testable behaviour — it is
documentation and an ADR, which `rebar explain plan` names as a legitimately test-free change class.
Verification is by the repository's existing documentation gates rather than by new tests, and the
acceptance criteria below name the command that checks each claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/adr/0097-many-to-many-tracker-projects.md` exists and records the store-ownership,
      event-free-migration, and conditional-stamp decisions with their rejected alternatives; checked
      by reading the file and confirming each of the three decisions names what it was chosen over.
- [ ] The Jira sync and config docs describe the project mapping and no longer present a single
      scalar project as the only option; checked by confirming no remaining passage states the
      single-project constraint as current behaviour.
- [ ] `docs/migrations.md` lists both new ensure units alongside the existing built-ins; checked by
      confirming each registered id appears in the doc.
- [ ] The docs state what the `multi-project-bridge` capability means for an older binary and what an
      operator does about it; checked by confirming the upgrade note names both the fail-closed
      behaviour and the remedy.
- [ ] The generated CLI reference includes `bridge projects`; checked by running the repository's
      documentation generation and confirming the verb appears without a manual edit.
